title: In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts, make the effect-coverage check recognise a test that lives
description:
In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts, make the effect-coverage check recognise a test that lives under a different filename than the module it exercises. One file, one concern.

ANCHOR, occurring exactly once, indented with six spaces on the const line:
      const candidates = [
        tf.replace(/\.tsx?$/, ".test.ts"),
        tf.replace(/^([^/]+\/[^/]+)\/src\//, "$1/test/").replace(/\.tsx?$/, ".test.ts"),
      ];

Keep those two candidate paths and the existing access-based loop exactly as they are: they are a correct fast path when they hit. Add a FALLBACK that runs only when neither candidate exists, so this change can never REDUCE reported coverage.

THE FALLBACK. Derive the vessel directory from the target path, which has the form repos/<vessel>/src/<rest>. Walk that vessel test directory recursively for files ending in .test.ts. Read each one and treat the target as covered if the file contains an import specifier whose FINAL PATH SEGMENT equals the target module basename, with an optional .js extension.

MATCH THE FULL SEGMENT, NOT A PREFIX. This is the load-bearing detail. For a target named gap.ts the specifier ending in /gap or /gap.js counts, while /gap-lifecycle-scan must NOT count. A prefix match would manufacture false coverage, and false coverage is strictly worse than false uncoverage here: this number feeds the recovery ladder rung that asks whether landed changes are known to do anything, so an over-reporting checker makes that rung assert something untrue. Anchor the comparison on a leading slash and require the segment to terminate at the quote or at .js.

Bound the work so a large vessel cannot stall a compose: skip the fallback entirely if the vessel test directory does not exist, cap the number of test files read at two hundred, and wrap the whole fallback so that any error leaves covered false rather than throwing.

WHY THIS IS CORRECT AND NOT MERELY GENEROUS. The most-rewritten file in this substrate reports as having no test file, while three test files exist whose names begin with its basename. Exactly one of those three actually imports it; the other two do not, and therefore do not exercise it. An import-based rule counts the one that does and correctly ignores the two that do not, which a filename-prefix rule would have miscounted as coverage. The rule asserts what it can verify: that some test loads this module.

Do not change what happens when a candidate path DOES exist, do not change the warning text or the counters, and edit no other file.
